en: The Ritual for Offering to the Ullambana (with Preface).
Formerly, the Dharma Master of Gushan composed a text for the Praise of the Ullambana Rite, wherein the Triple Gem and Maudgalyāyana together constitute six positions.
The *qibai* (prostration and confession) consists merely of four lines for each section. It originally employed the standard chanting used for inviting the Arhats;
later, Vinaya Master Zhenwu further chanted it as a ritual for the Indian patriarchs. Consequently, the *qǐqǐng* (invocation) was added and placed at the beginning of the hymn of praise.

The four lines concerning Mount Gushan have been moved here to serve as a hymn of praise for the Buddha. I maintain that when followers of the Śākya lineage observe the *Ullambana* rite, they must certainly, on behalf of both the living and the deceased, confess their transgressions and repent;
furthermore, the provision of offerings according to the sūtras must be preceded by the recitation of *adhiṣṭhāna-mantra* (vows of blessing).

These two elements are the most essential components of the Dharma assembly, yet in the past they were both omitted. Therefore, following the present hymn of praise for the Buddha, I shall now set forth the *adhiṣṭhāna-mantra* in accordance with the sūtra.

The Dharma. Furthermore, following the ritual of worship and praise, a separate text for repentance has been appended; all other matters remain as they were in the original tradition, with no further alterations made.

There are additions such as one hymn by Guifeng and verses for the exhortation [to the Buddhas], which are not included here according to precedent. These are simply the respective inclinations of each individual.
Recompiled by the Śramaṇa Yuanzhao of Yuhang.
(Entering the Dharma Hall for the first time. After performing three prostrations, they kneel with their right knees on the ground. They burn incense and scatter flowers. The leader chants:

We reverently acknowledge that the Muni, the Lord of Transformation, the Greatly Filial and Compassionate Honored One, has brought his meritorious practices through three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* to completion and is fully adorned with myriad virtues.
Whether in the causal stage or the resultant stage, he universally extols filial piety as his core principle; whether among the holy or the mundane, he regards repaying kindness as paramount.

He took this as his fundamental principle. Soon thereafter, having manifested auspicious signs at his birth in the royal palace, he renounced the golden wheel to enter the homeless life. Under the Bodhi tree, he realized the Truth;
he subdued the heavenly Māras and attained sagehood. He designated the three thousandfold world-system as his sphere of transformation and expounded the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates.
He personally ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to preach the Dharma for Queen Māyā, and he went in person to the kingdom of Kapilavastu to fulfill his filial duty by carrying his father’s coffin.

Beholding Maudgalyāyana’s lack of means to save his mother, he manifested the wondrous offering of the *almsgiving* (pravāraṇā) *Ullambana* rite. By arranging a hundred flavors upon the trays, he presented them as offerings to the Triple Gem;

by revering the majestic radiance of the sages and saints, he rescued both himself and others, whether living or deceased. Now, as the summer retreat draws to a close, I shall briefly present these humble delicacies to universally extend the ritual of offering, thereby repaying the debt of their arduous toil.

I only pray that— (Note: The text provided appears to be a fragment of a liturgical preface or inscription for a Buddhist memorial service, specifically the Ullambana festival. The final phrase "I only pray that—" indicates the sentence is incomplete.)
Now that the assembly of sages has descended together to this site of enlightenment to partake of our sincere offerings, may you deign to turn your radiant gaze toward us.
(After chanting, perform one prostration. Kneel again, holding the incense burner, and while meditating on the assembly of sages, recite the invitation:)

With single-minded devotion, I entreat Śākyamuni Buddha, the Teacher of the *Lanpen* (Ullambana) Sūtra who has long repaid his parental kindness, to descend to this sacred site and accept my offerings. (Three times; one prostration follows as below.)
With single-minded devotion, I reverently entreat the Sūtra-piṭaka of the Dharma-gate for Repaying Parents and Delivering Them from Suffering, the supreme teaching of the Lanpen (Ullambana).
With single-minded devotion, I reverently entreat the assembly of holy sages, bodhisattvas, and the Saṃgha who have attained the Way and exercise self-restraint throughout the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I invite the assembly of Pratyekabuddhas, the holy and worthy ones who have attained the Way and exercise self-mastery throughout the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I invite the assembly of Śrāvakas, the holy and worthy ones who have attained the Way and exercise self-mastery throughout the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, we respectfully invite the Venerable Maudgalyāyana, who repaid his parents' kindness, entered the Way, established the teachings, and benefited all living beings.
(Having invited him, they rise and extol the Triple Gem, chanting together in unison to invoke blessings.)
I prostrate to the True Teaching of Śākyamuni, The Eye of the Sages and Saints of the Three Vehicles, and to the Venerable Maudgalyāyana.
Now, receiving this teaching, I repay the boundless and profound kindness of my parents; May you, out of compassion, deign to hear these praises.
We each act to requite the infinite and deep debt of gratitude owed to our biological parents, Providing meals of a hundred flavors and the five fruits.
With fragrant oil and upright candles, I make offerings to the Triple Gem and the assembly of virtuous monks of the ten directions who observe the *pravāraṇā*.
May my present parents live for a hundred years, free from all suffering and affliction.

May my ancestors up to the seventh generation be liberated from the sufferings of the hungry ghosts (*preta*), be reborn among humans and devas, and enjoy boundless merit and happiness. May these benefits extend throughout the entire dharma-realm for immeasurable sentient beings.

Through this cultivation, both [the practitioner and the listeners] shall partake in benefit and joy. (Recite three times. Alternatively, one may further provide an exposition or recite the Buddha’s name and so forth as the occasion demands. Thereafter, perform prostrations and praises, chanting:)
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Teacher of the Ullambana Sūtra, who long repaid his parental kindness.
Having cultivated the path to sainthood through kalpas of practice, Maudgalyāyana entreated him with sorrow to expound the True Vehicle;
his father, the King, bowed in return from the midst of the void, and the Lord of the Field, hearing these words, was released from the net.
Cultivating causes and realizing fruits, all return to filial piety; transforming others and cultivating oneself exhaustively fulfills the vow to repay kindness.
May you turn your compassionate eyes toward all sentient beings, so that both the living and the deceased may receive this grace.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge and prostrate to you. (After chanting this together in harmony, perform three prostrations; the following sections are the same.)
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the *Ullambana Sūtra*, the supreme teaching for repaying one's parents and extracting them from suffering.
The Golden Mouth [of the Buddha] extensively expounded immeasurable teachings, yet this alone accords with the specific conditions for repaying one's parents;
it uniquely addresses the extraction of suffering by prescribing offerings to the *pravāraṇā* monks. Out of compassion, he further revealed the *Ullambana* method.
The joyful proclamation has been fully set forth; Dharma translated it so that the Way’s light would shine even more brightly.
King, ministers, nobles, and commoners alike all followed its practice. This wondrous instruction is as clear and bright as the sun and moon.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the assembly of the noble and holy Arhats and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions who have attained the Way and dwell in self-mastery.

Cultivating both compassion and wisdom, you are called a Great Being; Seeking the supreme above and transforming those below through kalpas, you save sentient beings by long riding the boat of the Six Perfections. Benefiting others, you reach the shore of the Three Emptinesses;
As inner realization approaches the realm of all Buddhas, You manifest in the form of a bhikṣu according to conditions.
Now that you have descended to this site of enlightenment, I pray that both the living and the deceased may all be freed from suffering.
With one mind, I prostrate to the assembly of noble sages who have attained the Way through self-mastery, as well as the community of Pratyekabuddhas throughout the ten directions.
Sharp wisdom is not derived from a teacher’s instruction; By contemplating dependent origination, one awakens to non-arising.
Proclaiming the Dharma and transmitting the lamp, they are called "followers of the lineage"; Cultivating the mind without a companion, they are likened to a rhinoceros.
Realizing emptiness suddenly as they watch flowers wither, They completely eliminate afflictions upon hearing the sound of bracelets.
Now that you have descended to this site of enlightenment, we pray that both the living and the deceased may all be freed from suffering.
With single-minded devotion, we pay homage to the assembly of Śrāvaka monks—the holy sages who have attained the Way and exercise self-mastery throughout the ten directions.
Dwelling in peace amidst mountain crags and beneath trees is superior; Through profound contemplation of the Four Noble Truths, the remnants of existence are exhausted.
The clamor of birth and death has been utterly overturned, And the tranquil mind of Nirvana has already been realized.
With mastery of the six supernormal powers, one transcends the realm of Māra; Wandering freely through the eight liberations, such a one is hailed as a Field of Merit.
Now that you have descended to this site of enlightenment, we pray that you may cause both the living and the deceased to leave suffering behind.
With one mind, we pay homage to the Venerable Maudgalyāyana, who entered the Way to repay his parents, established the teachings, and benefited all sentient beings.
Foremost in supernatural powers, dwelling in the state of no-more-learning, he left the home life to repay his filial debt to his parents.
Because it was difficult for his own power alone to eliminate the karmic retribution of his compassionate mother, he wailed in grief and subsequently followed the teachings of the Tathāgata.
He gave rise to subtle words to benefit future generations and extolled the Way of Filial Piety to profit all living beings.
Now that you have descended to this site of enlightenment, we pray that both the living and the deceased may all be freed from suffering.
(Having finished the praise, kneel facing one another and, while recollecting their living and deceased parents, repent with utmost sincerity and earnestness.)

I repent with a sincere heart. Our parents from whom we were born, and our kinsmen through many lifetimes, have turned their backs on the true and eternal, flowing long in the stream of birth and death.
Following the inverted perceptions of ignorance and clinging to objects of desire as conditions, they have unrestrainedly indulged the six sense-faculties, thereby committing the ten evil deeds:
greed, anger, and extreme views; killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct; and double-tongued speech, harsh words used for deception, and frivolous, false speech.

Their speech was deceptive and delusive. Furthermore, they were stingy with wealth, addicted to lust, intoxicated by wine, and obsessed with music. They insulted and humiliated monks and nuns, and treated the Buddha-Dharma with contempt.
They devoured the flesh and blood of sentient beings and maimed countless living spirits, yet they did not consider the calamities that would follow for ten thousand kalpas.
Yet, looking only to the beauty of the present moment, one may encounter calamities and hardships now, or suffer a fall into the depths of suffering later.
Having the honor of severing worldly attachments to leave the household life, it is only right that I cultivate my person to repay the virtue [of my parents].

Fortunate as I am to have encountered this day of the Buddha’s Joy and the time of the Sangha’s *prātimokṣa*, I look up to follow the Dharma-gate of the Tamer and formally offer the *Ullambana* alms-offering; however, because the ties of kinship are profound and the depth of my mournful longing is deep...

For this reason, I have briefly recounted these flaws and offer repentance on their behalf. Relying upon the majestic spiritual power and protection of the Triple Gem, and the hidden influence of the meritorious practices of the Sangha, may their roots of transgression be extinguished simultaneously.
May those who have passed away have their spirits transferred to the heavens, forever escaping the dark paths of the underworld;

and may those still living preserve their longevity in the human realm, remaining eternally free from illness and affliction, with their roots of goodness further strengthened and their right faith increased.

Profound! May all emerge together from saṃsāra and be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. With boundless compassion, may you universally cover all; where there is a response, may it be immediately realized.
We pray that you grant us your pity and graciously bestow upon us your protective mindfulness (three times).
Having finished the repentance, with a sincere heart take refuge and prostrate (after one person has chanted this, everyone performs one prostration and circumambulates while chanting):
Namo to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Namo to the Dharma of the ten directions. Namo to the Saṅgha of the ten directions.
Namo to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Teacher of the Ullambana Sūtra. Namo to the Ullambana Sūtra, the Ultimate Teaching.
Homage to the assembly of Bodhisattva Saṃghas of the ten directions who are self-reliant; homage to the assembly of Pratyekabuddha Saṃghas of the ten directions who are self-reliant;
homage to the assembly of Śrāvaka Saṃghas of the ten directions who are self-reliant; homage to the Venerable Maudgalyāyana, who repaid his parents' kindness and entered the Way.
(After reciting this three times while circumambulating, chant the *Ullambana Sūtra* or other sūtras as appropriate, and with utmost sincerity, disperse.)

The Ritual for Offering to the *Lanpen* (Ullambana) was rewritten by the Bhikṣu Zongju in the late summer of the Jiazi year of the Shaoxing era, with a request for donations to carve the printing blocks for its circulation.
May it serve to repent and cleanse the roots of transgression for one’s biological parents and all kinsmen throughout successive kalpas, thereby adorning the Pure Land.
